notes: The opening italic *This is* is split correctly: the construction-supplied copula joins the predicate nominal `סוֹף` under rule 20, while the supplied subject demonstrative *This* answers to no morpheme — the Hebrew writes no pronoun — and is `added`, rule 20 covering the copula and the presentative dummy and nothing more.

`כָּל־הָאָדָם` → *the whole ... of man* is read under rule 29's fronting case, the rectum being rendered anarthrously so its article takes the phrase's single written *the*, with the copula joining the predicate `כֹּל` discontinuously under rule 25.

*duty* is `added`: it names an obligation rather than expanding the quantifier, so it is not rule 19/31's supplied generic of the `כָּל־עֵץ` → *any kind of tree* kind. The competing reading, folding it into `כֹּל`'s unit still headed on *whole*, is named in that unit's note and remains defensible; the italic and the margin *this is the duty of all men* corroborate under rule 7 without deciding it.
